script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. A SUNNY SUBURBAN NEIGHBORHOOD - DAY

We open on a beautiful suburban neighborhood on a sunny afternoon. Children play in the streets, neighbors chat over their white picket fences. The scene is idyllic.

INT. JAMES' FAMILY ROOM - DAY

JAMES (mid 40s), a successful businessman, sits on the couch with his wife, LUCY (early 40s), and their teenage children, MARK (16) and EMMA (13). They all look comfortable and content.

LUCY
(to James)
You know what today is?

JAMES
(thinking)
What day is it?

LUCY
(smiling)
It's the day we adopted Mark and Emma 10 years ago.

The family shares a moment of nostalgia, looking at old family photos on the coffee table.

INT. JAMES' OFFICE - DAY

Later that day, James sits at his desk, staring at a computer screen filled with numbers and graphs. He looks tired and overwhelmed. His assistant, ANNA (late 20s), enters the room.

ANNA
(concerned)
Mr. James, you look tired. Is everything okay?

JAMES
(sighing)
It's just been a long week. I can't seem to catch a break.

ANNA
(placing a hand on his shoulder)
Why don't you take some time for yourself? Go home early today, spend some quality time with your family.

INT. JAMES' GARAGE - NIGHT

Later that evening, James works on a project in the garage. He hears the garage door open and turns to see Mark and Emma entering.

MARK
(excited)
Hey, Dad! We thought you'd want to see this.

Mark hands James a piece of paper covered in drawings.

JAMES
(smiling)
This is great, Mark! What is it?

MARK
(proudly)
It's a blueprint for a skate park we want to build in the vacant lot behind our school.

EMMA
(excitedly)
And I made some flyers to promote it!

James looks at the blueprint and the flyers, impressed by their creativity and dedication.

JAMES
(smiling)
This is fantastic, you two. I'm proud of you.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

The family gathers around the kitchen table, eating dinner together. They share stories about their day and laugh at each other's jokes.

LUCY
(to James)
You know, you're not getting any younger, James. It's important to take time for yourself and your family.

JAMES
(smiling)
I know, Lucy. And I'm grateful for every moment we have together.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

The next day, James attends a school board meeting to discuss the skate park proposal. He's nervous but determined to support Mark and Emma's project.

BOARD MEMBER
(skeptically)
And why should we invest in a skate park when there are more pressing issues in our community?

JAMES
(passionately)
Because this skate park will bring our community together. It will provide a safe and inclusive space for kids to express themselves and build meaningful relationships.

The board member is touched by James' words and agrees to support the project.

INT. FAMILY ROOM - NIGHT

Later that evening, James sits on the couch with his family, watching the news. They cheer as they see footage of the groundbreaking ceremony for the new skate park.

MARK
(proudly)
We did it, Dad!

JAMES
(smiling)
Yes, you did.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.

This is a modern, family-themed screenplay that explores the theme of identity through the experiences of a father, James, who rediscovers the importance of spending time with his family and supporting their passions. The story is original, adheres to the specified constraints, and includes proper screenplay format with INT/EXT scene headers, dialogue in uppercase character format, and realistic pacing.
